parole.significato: cantata (a vocal composition in several movements accompanied by instruments)
parole.testo: From Cantata (first attested in 1712), from Italian cantata (1638), from Medieval Latin cantata (1314), perfect passive participle of Latin canto (“to sing”)
Late 15th century, borrowed from Italian cappuccio (“hood, cowl”). Compare earlier Middle High German kabütze from Medieval Latin caputium. Doublet of Kappe, Kapuziner, and Cappuccino.

From older Tartuffel or Tartüffel (18th c.), from Italian tartufolo, diminutive of tartufo (“truffle”), from Medieval Latin *territūberum or Latin terrae tūber (“tuber of the earth”). parole.significato: corsair, pirate (one who plunders at sea) (of male or unspecified sex)

Borrowed from Italian partitura (“partition, musical score”), from Medieval Latin partitūra, from partiō, partior (“to divide, to partition, to share”) + -ūra.
From Italian smalto, from Medieval Latin smaltum, from Frankish *smalt. Doublet of Schmalz.

parole.significato: a small or loose piece of paper, slip
parole.testo: From Early New High German zeddel, zedel, from Middle High German zëdele, zëdel, a loan from Italian cedola, from Medieval Latin cedula, schedula, the diminutive of scheda, scida (“strip of papyrus”) ultimately from Ancient Greek σχίδη (skhídē, “splinter, fragment”). parole.testo: A distortion of the Italian silermontano, sciarmontano, from Medieval Latin siser montanum, also found as French sermontain.
